brief: Overnight global equities de-risked from AI-capex and AI-financing exposure: QQQ -0.7%, Asia's MSCI -1.7%, Korea's Kospi -6.2% on AI-buildout durability and financing worries, higher borrowing costs and Chinese memory competition (CXMT); megacaps stayed more resilient (Meta +3.4%, Apple +1.3%, Microsoft +1.0%). Broadcom CEO Hock Tan said compute demand still outruns supply through 2028-29 into 2030, citing OpenAI's ~$50bn annualised revenue as evidence of real demand, but argued capital, not chips or power, is now the binding constraint as wafer and memory shortages ease; the desk says press coverage focused on his investor skepticism, out of context versus his demand comments. The resulting memory squeeze is hitting consumer hardware: smartphone shipments -20% y/y (lowest since 2012) and PC shipments -22.4%, with DRAM costs up fivefold y/y. The clear positive was Meta's Muse Wonder launch, ranking just behind Claude Opus 5.5 on Artificial Analysis' Intelligence Index, lifting Meta shares. Also covered: Publicis's Q4 organic growth beat (Sapient turning positive is the swing factor), a Neutral initiation on CTS Eventim, and GS's constructive-vs-cautious split on payments names into Q3 earnings.
